title: Where gadgets go when they die
text: {{1}} theory, electronic waste ought to be the easiest treasure on Earth: old phones and laptops {{2}} packed with gold, silver and copper — a tonne of circuit boards is far richer {{3}} a tonne of mined ore — and every gadget contains materials worth recovering. In practice only about a fifth {{4}} formally collected and recycled. The rest sleeps in drawers, and a worrying share leaks into soil and rivers {{5}} it is dumped carelessly or torn apart in informal scrapyards, {{6}} cables are burnt in the open to free the metal inside. Regulators are responding {{7}} right-to-repair laws that push manufacturers towards longer-lasting, repairable designs, and the best e-waste policy may be the simplest one: make gadgets {{8}} last longer in the first place.
